procedure.description: neuroplasty and/or transposition, median nerve at carpal tunnel

denial.carcText: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer.
denial.text: Saltmarsh Benefits Administrators denied the claim for CPT 64721 (neuroplasty and/or transposition, median nerve at carpal tunnel) with date of service 2026-05-31. CARC 50: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer. Payer remark: Documentation does not establish failure of conservative treatment or electrodiagnostic confirmation.

criteria.text: Symptoms consistent with carpal tunnel syndrome, such as nocturnal paresthesias in the median nerve distribution with a positive Tinel or Phalen sign, present for at least 6 weeks.
Failure of at least 6 weeks of conservative management including neutral wrist splinting, together with NSAIDs, activity modification, or a corticosteroid injection.
Electrodiagnostic testing (nerve conduction study or electromyography) confirming median neuropathy at the wrist, unless thenar atrophy or constant sensory loss is present.

chart.text: Here with a cough and congestion for 4 days, low grade temp at home, no shortness of breath. Lungs clear, throat a little red, ears fine. Looks viral. Fluids, rest, honey for the cough, come back if she gets a fever over 101 or it goes past two weeks.

Referral letter from the primary care office. Thank you for seeing this patient of mine for surgical evaluation. Her history and medication list are attached. Please let me know what you recommend and whether anything is needed from our end for clearance.

56 year old woman here for the left hand, referred by the PCP. Works on a keyboard all day. Discussed carpal tunnel release, open versus endoscopic, recovery. Her history otherwise: hypothyroidism on levothyroxine, reflux on omeprazole as needed, hypertension on lisinopril. Surgeries: a C-section. Allergies: no drug allergies. Does not smoke, a glass of wine on weekends, works in a warehouse. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. 4 months of numbness and tingling in the thumb, index, and middle fingers on the left, wakes her at night, shakes it out. Positive Tinel at the left wrist, Phalen positive in about 20 seconds. Some early thenar weakness, no atrophy yet. Splinted at night for 9 weeks, naproxen twice a day, moved the mouse to the other hand, and had a steroid shot in the left carpal tunnel from the PCP that helped for about three weeks and wore off.
Thyroid labs back. TSH 3.1, free T4 normal. No change to the levothyroxine 100. Repeat in a year.

Nerve conduction study, left upper extremity. Median sensory peak latency 4.3 milliseconds across the wrist, prolonged. Median motor distal latency 5.9 milliseconds, prolonged. Ulnar normal. Consistent with moderate left median neuropathy at the wrist.
Seasonal allergies acting up, itchy eyes, sneezing, clear drainage, worse outdoors. No wheeze. Cetirizine at night and the saline rinse. Fine with that.

Low back strain after moving furniture over the weekend. No radiation down the legs, no numbness, no bowel or bladder trouble. Paraspinal tenderness, straight leg raise negative. Heat, keep moving, ibuprofen with food for a week. Should settle.
Back to review the plan for the left hand. Still symptomatic. Wants to proceed. Vitals today 112 over 90, pulse 76.
Optometry report forwarded for the record. Routine refraction, mild astigmatism, new glasses prescribed, retinas healthy, pressures 16 and 19. No ocular pathology noted.

Knee pain going down stairs, right side, no injury, no locking or giving way. Patellar grind positive, no effusion, ligaments stable. Patellofemoral pain. Quad strengthening sheet, ice after activity, cushioned shoes.
Vitamin D came back 17. Started 1000 units daily, recheck in three months. Also talked about calcium from food rather than pills.
Message from the patient about scheduling. Wants a date in the next couple of months if the insurance comes through. Passed to the surgery scheduler.
Follow-up. Same story, no better. She asked about timing around work and family, we talked through it. Still wants to proceed.

Annual physical. Feels well overall. Sleeping fine, appetite fine, no chest pain, no shortness of breath. Flu shot given in the left arm today. Due for a tetanus booster, she will think about it. Labs ordered, fasting.
Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.
Gastroenterology note received. Screening colonoscopy completed, two small polyps removed, benign on pathology, repeat in 5 years.

Trouble sleeping for a couple of months, falls asleep fine but wakes at three and lies there. No snoring per the spouse, no daytime naps, two cups of coffee before noon. Went over sleep hygiene, no screens in bed, cut the afternoon caffeine. Will hold off on medication for now.
Patient called about a tick bite on the scalp after a hike. Tick removed whole, no rash, no fever. Watch for a bull's-eye rash or flu symptoms over the next month and call if either shows up.
Pharmacy called about the refill on the omeprazole 20. Approved 90 days. She mentioned the heartburn is better since cutting back on coffee.
Blood pressure check. 141 over 77 today, 130 over 85 on repeat. She has been taking the lisinopril 20 most days, admits to missing weekends. Low salt talk again. Keep the dose, recheck in 8 weeks.

Called her with the cholesterol results. Total 195, LDL 155, HDL 50, triglycerides 123. Discussed diet and walking. She wants to try lifestyle first for six months before we talk about a statin. Agreed.
Work note requested for a sick day last Tuesday. Faxed to the employer.
Mammogram report forwarded for the record. Bilateral screening, BI-RADS 1, negative, routine screening in one year.

Mole on the right calf that her spouse noticed. About 7 millimeters, even color, regular border, no change she is aware of. Looks benign. Photo in the chart for comparison, recheck in a year or sooner if it changes.
A1c came back 6.2. Prediabetic range, same as last year. Walking program, cut the soda, recheck in six months. She is motivated.
Pre-op. Consent signed for left open carpal tunnel release under local with sedation. Marked.

Twisted the right ankle stepping off a curb 6 days ago. Swelling over the lateral malleolus, tender over the ATFL, can bear weight. Ottawa negative, no film. Brace, ice, ibuprofen, elevate. Should be fine in a couple weeks.

expected.note: The chart documents every criterion; the CARC 50 denial can be answered from the record.
